table1.title: Table 1 | Scientific model inventory in the v0.1.1 runtime
table1.note: “Anchored” denotes a literature-recognizable model family, not independent biological validation of the NeuroLab implementation.
rows: Coupled excitatory/inhibitory population dynamics; time-constant units are not interpreted physiologically unless explicitly specified.
Coupled phase oscillators; ω is an angular-frequency variable and should not be conflated with frequency in Hz.
Mean-reverting stochastic baseline with optional coupling.
Six-state cortical-column structure with NeuroLab numerical scaling/safeguards; not claimed as a canonical parameter set.
Diffusively coupled normal-form oscillator network used as a whole-brain-style dynamical model [26, 27].
Discrete linear stochastic dynamics; engineering/statistical comparator rather than physiological model.
Stable vector autoregressive dynamics; coefficients are model-derived and not anatomical connectivity by default.
Markov-switching ROI/BOLD time-series proxy; not a complete HMM inference pipeline.
Complex-amplitude oscillator with phase-lagged network coupling and deterministic/stochastic drive.
Regime-switching linear dynamics; not an exact reproduction of a specific HMM inference framework.
Wong–Wang-inspired recurrent ROI model with a compact BOLD-like smoothing transform; not a full hemodynamic forward model [28].

table4.title: Table 4 | Positioning of NeuroLab OS relative to complementary research-software ecosystems
table4.note: The comparison describes primary design emphasis and does not imply feature exclusivity or superiority.
rows: Mature EEG/MEG preprocessing, analysis and visualization
NeuroLab uses a narrower signal workflow and connects it to model review, fitting and provenance.
Standardized data organization and executable app conventions
NeuroLab is BIDS-lite-oriented for EEG but does not claim full BIDS/NWB conformance.
Distributed versioning of data, code and their relationships
NeuroLab focuses on run-level preprocessing/model/report lineage inside the application.
Whole-brain network simulation and personalized modelling
NeuroLab exposes a smaller heterogeneous model registry integrated with QC/fitting/reporting.
Flexible model definition, performance and analysis
NeuroLab is not a simulator programming framework; it emphasizes researcher-facing model contracts and workflow continuity.
Common objects and operations for time-resolved neuroscience data
NeuroLab is less general as a data-analysis library and instead couples data handling to reviewed modelling and report lineage.
NeuroLab targets neural time-series modelling and provenance rather than calcium-imaging workflow consensus.
